extraction.name: CIFAR-10 airbench
extraction.description: A set of training methods for CIFAR-10 which reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. The paper introduces a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation (alternating flip) and releases training scripts as the airbench Python package.
extraction.creator: Keller Jordan
extraction.citeAs: Jordan, Keller. '94% on CIFAR-10 in 3.29 Seconds on a Single GPU.' arXiv preprint arXiv:2404.00498 (2024).
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes, divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images. The dataset was originally collected by Krizhevsky et al. (2009).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-10 dataset (Krizhevsky et al., 2009): 60,000 32x32 color images labeled as one of ten classes, sourced from http://www.cs.toronto.edu/~kriz/cifar.html
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data augmentation includes random horizontal flipping (or alternating flip as proposed), 2-pixel random translation using reflection padding, and optionally 12-pixel Cutout augmentation. Test-time augmentation (TTA) includes horizontal flipping and two extra crops, creating six augmented views per test image.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images are loaded as uint8, converted to half precision (fp16) and normalized using CIFAR mean (0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465) and std (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616). The first convolutional layer is initialized as a patch-whitening transformation using the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of 2x2 patches across the training distribution. Images are pre-padded for random translation augmentation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code is released at https://github.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench and as the airbench Python package (pip install airbench). Multiple versioned scripts are released: airbench94_compiled.py, airbench94.py, airbench95.py, and airbench96.py.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Faster training methods reduce the computational cost of machine learning research on CIFAR-10, enabling researchers to conduct large-scale studies (e.g., involving millions of trained networks) with fewer resources, and accelerating experimental iteration time.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The training methods were developed solely with the goal of maximizing training speed on CIFAR-10. Runtimes are measured on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU and may differ on other hardware. The compiled variant (airbench94_compiled.py) has a one-time compilation cost of up to several minutes, making it only beneficial when many runs are executed at once.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking neural networks on CIFAR-10. Intended to accelerate research projects involving CIFAR-10, reduce cost of experiments requiring large numbers of trained networks, and enable rapid accumulation of statistical significance for hyperparameter comparisons. Also evaluated on CIFAR-100, SVHN, and CINIC-10 for generalization testing.
